title: Sausages & Mash with Onion Gravy
subtitle: browned mild pork sausages on creamy mashed potatoes, smothered in a rich, sweet onion gravy, with peas
imageAlt: Browned sausages on mashed potatoes with brown onion gravy and green peas on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Three pans going at once: potatoes, sausages and gravy. Start the potatoes first.

items.name: russet potatoes
items.note: peeled and cut in 5 cm chunks

steps.title: Potatoes on
steps.text: Cover the potatoes with cold water in a large pot, add a big pinch of salt, bring to a boil and simmer 15–18 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.

steps.title: Onions
steps.text: Meanwhile, melt the 2 tbsp butter in a medium skillet over medium. Add the onions and brown sugar and cook 12–15 minutes, stirring often, until soft and deep golden.

steps.title: Sausages
steps.text: At the same time, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-low. Cook the sausages 15–18 minutes, turning often, until browned all over and 71°C (160°F) in the centre.

steps.title: Gravy
steps.text: Sprinkle the flour over the onions and stir 1 minute. Slowly stir in the broth, then the Worcestershire, dried thyme, pepper and salt, and simmer 4–5 minutes until thick.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Drain the potatoes and let them steam dry 1 minute. Mash with the 3 tbsp butter, warm milk and salt until smooth.

steps.title: Peas
steps.text: Microwave the peas, covered, with a splash of water 3–4 minutes until hot.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Mash on each plate, sausages on top, gravy over everything, peas on the side.

fixIt.fix: The heat was too high. Keep it medium-low and don't prick them.
Don't use a blender or overwork it; mash by hand and add the milk warm.
Give the onions longer; their colour is the gravy's colour. A splash more Worcestershire helps.

saleTip: No Frills sausages are often 2 packs for $10; freeze them raw in their tray.
swap: Mild Italian, honey garlic or breakfast sausages all work; cook pork or beef sausages to 71°C (160°F), chicken or turkey to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Slice leftover sausages into the gravy and reheat together; mash reheats with a splash of milk.
doneness: Pork sausages at 71°C (160°F) in the centre (Health Canada, ground pork). Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested British bangers and mash methods (BBC Good Food, Canadian Living): sausages pan-cooked slowly over medium-low, buttery mash, and a gravy from slowly browned onions, flour and beef stock.
prepAhead: Make the onion gravy up to 3 days ahead.
Mashed potatoes keep 3 days; reheat with a splash of milk.
reheat: Sausages and gravy covered in the microwave 2–3 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Sausages, mash and a simple onion gravy; no dried thyme or peas.

fancy.note: Old cheddar folded into the mash.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: fold the cheddar into the hot mash at the end.

plating: A big swoosh of mash across the plate.
Sausages leaning on it, gravy poured over.

why.2-1: Onions cooked low and slow turn sweet and brown, which flavours the whole gravy.
why.1-0: Gentle heat lets sausages cook through before the casings burst.
why.0-2: Warm milk keeps the mash fluffy; cold milk makes it gluey.

funFact: Sausages are called 'bangers' in Britain because wartime sausages, packed with water, often burst with a bang in the pan.

keeps.note: freeze sausages in gravy; mash freezes well too
